results.evidence: The 1946 first-ascent account gives an 800 ft, 50-degree ice couloir. The only source for the itinerary's '50-60 degrees with one 70-degree step' (and max_angle 70) is a single July 3, 2009 party (its SummitPost and NWHikers reports share one author): 'starts out around 50 degrees, steepening to 60 at the top (with one 70 degree step at the transition to rock)'. No second independent party gives an angle; the 2013 CascadeClimbers report only says conditions were snowy. The couloir angle plausibly varies with snow cover, so neither 45-50 nor 50-60/70 can be adopted on two sources. What would settle it: a second independent trip report or guide stating the couloir's top angle.

The 2009 party reports 'about ten 60m raps to the glacier below', and the 2013 party (a different team) says they made double-rope rappels the whole way, which is consistent with rappels longer than 30 m, but gives neither count nor rope length. No source states per-rappel lengths or supports the 30 m cap in rappel_detail and rappel_count_note, and none explicitly refutes it. What would settle it: a report stating the rope length used and the approximate length of each rappel.

Dated ascents from independent parties run from June into late August: June 10, 2013 (CascadeClimbers), July 3, 2009 (SummitPost), July 5, 1946 (FA, AAJ), July 23, 2023, Aug 25, 2007 and Aug 28, 2006 (CascadeClimbers titles). This supports the Jun-Aug season and contradicts the 'mid-July' start in best_season, seasonal_guidance and climate. But whether September belongs in the window rests on one unverified search snippet of a September 2018 Peakbagger ascent, and 'reliable window' is a judgment no source states. So neither side can be rewritten on two agreeing sources. What would settle it: a verified September ascent report (or a guide stating the window), after which best_season/optimalWindow/climate.typical could be aligned with the season column.
